# Method 1: Using power.t.test (same as candidate)
cat("=== METHOD 1: power.t.test ===\n")
pw_n40 <- power.t.test(
  n = 40,
  delta = mean_increase,
  sd = sd,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)
pw_n41 <- power.t.test(
  n = 41,
  delta = mean_increase,
  sd = sd,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

cat("Power at n=40:", pw_n40$power, "\n")
cat("Power at n=41:", pw_n41$power, "\n")
cat("Minimum n achieving 80% power:", ifelse(pw_n41$power >= 0.8, 41, 40), "\n\n")

# Method 2: Manual calculation using non-central t-distribution
# For one-sample t-test:
# Non-centrality parameter: lambda = sqrt(n) * delta / sd = sqrt(n) * mean_increase / sd
# Critical value: t_crit = t_{alpha, n-1} for one-sided test
# Power = P(T > t_crit | H1), where T ~ t(df=n-1, lambda)

cat("=== METHOD 2: Manual non-central t approach ===\n")

calculate_power_manual <- function(n, delta, sigma, sig_level) {
  # Non-centrality parameter
  lambda <- sqrt(n) * delta / sigma
  
  # Critical value (one-sided, right tail)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - sig_level, df = n - 1)
  
  # Power: P(T > t_crit) where T ~ t(df, lambda)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = n - 1, ncp = lambda)
  return(power)
}

# Critical value: t_crit = t_{alpha, n-1} for one-sided test
# Power = P(T > t_crit | H1), where T ~ t(df=n-1, lambda)

# Evidence e1; success=true

library(stats)

# Study parameters
mean_increase <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80

# Effect size (Cohen's d)
cohens_d <- mean_increase / sd
cat("Cohen's d =", cohens_d, "\n")

# For a one-sample t-test, we need to find the minimum n such that power >= 0.80
# We'll use power.t.test from the stats package
# For one-sample t-test: delta is the effect size (mean under H1 - mean under H0)
# in units of SD, so delta = cohens_d

# Power analysis function for one-sample t-test
# power.t.test(n=NULL, delta, sd=1, sig.level, power, type="one.sample", alternative="one.sided")

# Try different sample sizes to find the minimum
power_results <- data.frame()

for (n in 1:200) {
  pw <- power.t.test(
    n = n,
    delta = mean_increase,
    sd = sd,
    sig.level = alpha,
    type = "one.sample",
    alternative = "one.sided"
  )
  power_results <- rbind(power_results, data.frame(
    n = n,
    power = pw$power
  ))
}

# Find minimum n achieving target power
min_n_idx <- which(power_results$power >= target_power)[1]
min_n <- power_results$n[min_n_idx]
achieved_power <- power_results$power[min_n_idx]

# Also get power at n-1 for comparison
power_at_n_minus_1 <- power_results$power[min_n_idx - 1]

cat("\nSample Size Analysis:\n")
cat("Minimum n achieving 80% power:", min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", achieved_power, "\n")
cat("Power at n =", min_n - 1, ":", power_at_n_minus_1, "\n")

# Verify with direct calculation
pw_verify <- power.t.test(
  n = min_n,
  delta = mean_increase,
  sd = sd,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

cat("\nVerification:\n")
cat("Power at n =", min_n, ":", pw_verify$power, "\n")

# Output results
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n, unit = "participants_total"),
      list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(achieved_power, 6), unit = "probability"),
      list(metric = "cohens_d", value = cohens_d, unit = "standardized_effect_size"),
      list(metric = "power_at_n_minus_1", value = round(power_at_n_minus_1, 6), unit = "probability")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)
